clue.text: Flag during exam? Jumbo may provide diversion for me

definitions.text: Jumbo may provide diversion for me

indicators.note: during places the flag word in the middle of the exam word, splitting it open

parts.note: Highers are the Scottish school-leaving exams, so an exam can be a Higher
a jack is a small flag flown at a ship's bow, as in Union Jack

explanation.surface: A student puzzles over a flag question in an exam, then a riddle about jumbo jets.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a jumbo jet may be diverted by its seizer, who speaks as 'me'. The Higher is a Scottish exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A hijacker seizes an aircraft, such as a jumbo jet, and forces it to fly elsewhere; this is a variant spelling.

clue.text: Help boy rambling to restrict hesitation and exaggeration

indicators.note: to restrict means to hem in, so the hesitation sound is held inside the jumbled letters
rambling suggests wandering about aimlessly, so the letters of help boy are jumbled

parts.note: er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: A rambling helper is told to cut out the ums and stop overstating things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' makes HYPBOLE from the letters of help boy, and 'to restrict' holds the hesitation sound in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperbole is the figure of speech that overstates for effect, a direct synonym of exaggeration.

clue.text: Wellington's mounted attack finally unhorsed army general

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means climbing upward, so the word for attack reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to mug is to attack and rob someone

indicators.note: unhorsed means losing the horse; H is slang shorthand for heroin, called horse, and it is removed from the final position

parts.note: William Booth founded the Salvation Army and was its first General

explanation.surface: The Duke of Wellington leads a cavalry charge that ends with a general thrown from his horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' reverses MUG to GUM. General Booth led the Salvation Army; 'finally unhorsed' takes off his last letter H (horse is slang for heroin, H). The 's is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellington is a waterproof rubber boot, named after the Duke; a gumboot is another name for the same footwear.

clue.text: Learning to dispense with queen after a trial

indicators.note: after places the trimmed learning word behind the letter A
to dispense with means to do without, so the queen's letters are taken out

parts.note: erudition is deep scholarly learning
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A student gives up royal ambitions after an audition-like test of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dispense with' takes the Queen's cipher out of the learning word; 'after' puts what is left behind A. ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: An audition is a trial performance given by an actor or musician seeking a part.

clue.text: Slug commonly found in joint of meat and buffet snack

parts.note: a knuckle of pork or veal is a cut from the joint at the leg
a sandwich is a typical snack laid out at a buffet

explanation.surface: Someone finds a garden slug lurking in the meat and sandwiches at a buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slug' looks like the garden creature but is a punch; 'commonly' marks the answer as slang. 'buffet' also hints at hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A knuckle sandwich is a slang term for a punch in the mouth, and to slug someone is to punch them.

clue.text: Give account of troops no longer alive

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British Army troops
the late someone is a person recently deceased

explanation.surface: A survivor reports on soldiers who have died in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to narrate or tell it, giving an account of events.

clue.text: Beat in game after suffering setback

indicators.note: a setback sends something backwards, so the name of the game reads in reverse

parts.note: golf is a game played with clubs on a course

explanation.surface: A player wins a game after recovering from an early reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' in the surface sounds like winning, but it means to thrash; the game name GOLF reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog someone is to beat them with a whip or stick.

clue.text: Promote rapidly taking firm line

parts.note: fast means firmly fixed, as in stuck fast
a track is a line, as a railway line or a path

explanation.surface: A company boss is moved up quickly for taking a firm line on policy.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast-track someone is to advance them faster than the usual route, an idiom for quick promotion.

clue.text: What superintendent will do having finished with witness

parts.note: over means ended, as in the match is over
to witness something is to see it

explanation.surface: A police superintendent considers what to do once a witness has been questioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A superintendent supervises people and work, which is exactly what it means to oversee them.

clue.text: Grandeur I associated with a mostly determined statesman

parts.note: pomp is splendid ceremonial display, grandeur

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter of the word for determined is dropped

parts.note: dour can mean stubborn and determined, an old sense of the word

explanation.surface: Grand ceremony is linked with a stubborn politician.
explanation.walkthrough: DOUR loses its last letter to give DOU. Georges Pompidou was President of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Pompidou was a French prime minister and later President, a leading statesman of the 1960s and 70s.

clue.text: Contract, for example, that's verbal

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the word for an example is said aloud and gives a word sounding the same

parts.note: an example made of someone serves as a lesson to others

explanation.surface: A lawyer offers a spoken agreement as an example of a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun for a legal agreement but is the verb meaning shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract is to shrink or reduce, and to lessen is to make or become less.

clue.text: Man is not at first a criminal

indicators.note: not at first means the first letter is missing from the word for a criminal

parts.note: a crook is a criminal, a swindler or thief

explanation.surface: A man claims he was not a criminal at the beginning of his career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece, not a person. 'is' and 'a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the pieces are called men, and the rook, or castle, is one of them.

clue.text: Like work producing carpet?

parts.note: to take to something is to come to like it
a task is a piece of work

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of work goes into making a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' is the verb: to call someone in and reprimand them, from being summoned 'on the carpet'.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to scold them severely, the same as to reprimand or rebuke.

clue.text: Excuse said to be forthright

parts.note: an out is an excuse or way of escape, as in giving oneself an out
spoken means said aloud

explanation.surface: A spoken excuse is offered in a frank, direct manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forthright speaks frankly and directly, which is what outspoken means.

clue.text: I despise wife prepared to make jibe when passing

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A husband who cannot stand his wife plans a cutting remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideswipe is a critical remark made in passing, an incidental dig at someone.

clue.text: Not be sure of state at conclusion of interview

indicators.note: at here means positioned at, so the word for state sits at the close of the answer
the conclusion of a word is its last letter

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A candidate is uncertain what to say at the end of a job interview.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' places the word for state at the end, after the last letter of interview.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver is to hesitate or be undecided, unable to settle on a choice.

clue.text: US resort abandoned before European turned up in Nice

indicators.note: before puts the jumbled letters ahead of the letter for European
abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: An American resort is abandoned before a European arrives in the French city of Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges USRESORT to RETROUSS. 'Nice' is the French city, so the definition calls for a French word; 'turned up' describes a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Retroussé is French for turned up, used in English of a nose that tilts upward at the tip.

clue.text: Sack architect finally given blame for dangerous building

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them from a job

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word architect

parts.note: a rap is blame or punishment, as in take the rap

explanation.surface: An architect is sacked and blamed for designing an unsafe building.
explanation.definitionFit: A firetrap is a building that would be dangerous in a fire, lacking safe exits.

clue.text: Gradually destroy characters Dumbledore's about to protect

indicators.note: about means turning round, so the hidden letters are read backwards
characters means letters, here letters of the word Dumbledore's
to protect means to shield inside, so the run of letters is held within Dumbledore's

explanation.surface: The wizard Dumbledore is about to protect his young charges from slow destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside Dumbledore's lies EDORE; 'about' turns it round. Dumbledore is the headmaster in the Harry Potter books.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as water wears down rock.

clue.text: Knowledge of literature gained from university

definitions.meaning: someone of wide ... has a broad knowledge of books
An English town with a university

explanation.definitionFit: A well-read person's learning comes from their reading; Reading is also a university town west of London.

clue.text: Man one has to avoid in woman's clothing

parts.note: Max is a man's name
I is the Roman numeral for one
to skirt something is to go round it, avoiding it

explanation.surface: A man has to keep out of sight disguised in women's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxiskirt is a long skirt reaching to the ankles, a garment worn by women.

clue.text: Popular time to drink beer for smoker

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: to drink means to take in, so the word for time holds the beer inside it

parts.note: hr is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: In a popular pub it is time for a smoker to have a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoker' looks like a person who smokes a pipe, but the definition is anyone who breathes in; 'to drink' signals the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler is one who breathes in, as a smoker draws in smoke.

clue.text: Commons healthier for including these politicians?

definitions.meaning: commons are open land shared by a village
a diet is healthier for including leafy vegetables, which share their name with members of the Green Party

explanation.definitionFit: Village greens are common land; green vegetables are healthy; and members of the Green Party are politicians known by the same plural name.

clue.text: Game of crib started by men into jazz

indicators.note: started by means the crib word comes after the word for the jazz fans, which begins the answer

parts.note: cats is slang for jazz enthusiasts or musicians
a crib is a baby's bed, a cradle

explanation.surface: Jazz musicians start up a game of cribbage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crib' suggests the card game cribbage but means a baby's bed. Cat's cradle is a string game.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's cradle is a children's game of making patterns with a loop of string between the fingers.

clue.text: Drive away from film before it has finished

indicators.note: before it has finished means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: to shoot is to film a scene

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a film before it is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive away' looks like a car journey but means to chase off.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is said to drive away animals or people, as in shooing chickens out of the yard.

clue.text: Beam about current one being as good as gold

definitions.text: one being as good as gold

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for beam goes round the current symbol

parts.note: to beam is to smile broadly
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone beams about a child who is being as good as gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile compares one thing to another with 'as' or 'like', and 'as good as gold' is a stock example.

clue.text: Serials broadcast involving island people from the Med?

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the island letter is placed within the jumbled letters
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of serials are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: TV serials are broadcast featuring island people from around the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges SERIALS to ISRAELS, and 'involving' puts I in before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Israelis are the people of Israel, a country on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A beast is so, on its back

indicators.note: on its back means lying turned over, so the word for so is reversed

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, meaning so

explanation.surface: A beast is lying helpless on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monstrous giant of folklore, a brutish beast.

clue.text: He picks out clothing for every dog

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping round, so the jumbled letters go around the word for each
out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of he picks are rearranged

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: A man selects clothes for each member of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of he picks to SCHIPKE, and 'clothing' wraps that round the word for each. The breed is Belgian, a barge dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A schipperke is a small black Belgian breed of dog.
